summary: You have new medicines, two blood tests, an eye doctor referral, and a visit back in 3 months. You told us getting there is hard and you are not sure about insurance. Below are steps to get coverage, find a low-cost clinic close to you in Columbus, and plan your lab trip. We did not find a verified ride program near you, so a person should help with transportation.

steps.title: Check if you can get Medicaid
steps.action: Apply for Medicaid. It can give free or low-cost health coverage to adults with low income. If you get it, it may help pay for your medicines, blood tests, and eye doctor visit. Once you have coverage, ask the program if it offers rides to medical visits.
steps.why: Your new medicines and tests cost money. Coverage can make them free or cheaper.

steps.title: Find a low-cost clinic close to home
steps.action: Franklin Station Health Center is about 0.7 km from you, which may be a short walk. These health centers charge based on your income, even if you have no insurance. Call and ask: Can you help me sign up for Medicaid? Can you help with low-cost medicine? Do you do blood tests here?
steps.why: A nearby clinic means a shorter trip. It can help you afford metformin and lisinopril and help with coverage.

steps.title: Get your fasting blood test in the next 2 weeks
steps.action: Your paper says to go to any Quest or Labcorp lab within 2 weeks. Do not eat before the test. Pick the lab closest to you or on your bus line. Go early in the morning so fasting is easier. Ask the lab about cost before your test if you have no insurance.
steps.why: This test checks your kidneys after your medicine changes.

steps.title: Plan for the eye doctor visit
steps.action: The eye doctor's office will call you to set up a time. If no one calls in 10 days, call the number on your paper. When they call, ask where the office is and if it is near a bus line. Ask what it will cost without insurance.
steps.why: Diabetes can harm your eyes. This check catches problems early.

steps.title: Take your medicines the new way
steps.action: Take metformin 1 pill two times a day with food. Take 2 lisinopril pills (20 mg) once a day. Stop taking ibuprofen (Advil). If you need a pain medicine, ask your clinic or pharmacist what is safe.
steps.why: These changes protect your blood sugar, blood pressure, and kidneys.

steps.title: Know when to get help fast
steps.action: Call the office if your blood sugar is over 300 two times in a row. Call 911 for chest pain, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness on one side of your body.
steps.why: These signs can be serious and need quick care.
